The DiRT franchise is having an identity crisis.

On the one hand, it wants to be a simulation game.
On the other, it wants to be an arcade game.

Physics in this game is worse than any other game of the series, with absolutely terrible controller options that do not make the game fun. Throttle control? Forget about it. No matter what setting you choose, 50% is full throttle. This isn't how real gas pedals work, so why force this mechanic? It makes it incredibly difficult to actually control your car, especially on pavement - which this game simulates the WORST. Don't even get me started with this "always online career" crap. Do better Codemasters, you used to be a legendary studio.

I'll stick to the old games in this franchise... glad I only spend $5 on this one.

An amazing sequel to the original Dirt Rally. Graphics are beautiful, nice selection of cars and tracks to choose from, easily customized controls (playing on controller). One thing I found that made the game way more enjoyable is how much less your car gets clipped on the edges of the track. Original Dirt Rally was less forgiving and made it very frustrating as a new player. While some tracks are still tough, with high snow banks as an example, it is improved greatly and doesn't leave me rage quitting as it did in the original.
It's a good follow-up to Dirt Rally 1. The DLC price policy is a bit wonky, but they are working on and improving the game, so I'm good with that.

I played DiRT 2.0 on Xbox Box Game Pass for about 10 hours before buying the Steam GOTY edition. This is by far the best rally sim on the market at the moment and well worth your money. This is certainly no arcade racer and you will experience intense frustration at hardly being able to complete a stage let alone win when you first start playing. The satisfaction at slowly progressing and learning each vehicle is well worth the hair pulling.

My favourite aspect of the game are the daily and weekly community events and challenges. I do however recommend buying all the DLC as many of those events you will be unable to play with the base game. The DLC is quite costly but wait for a sale and pick up the GOTY edition DiRT cheap like I did.

Riding on the redline, you approach a corner at too great a speed. Your co-driver thinks you're a fool, but being pre-programmed he cannot voice his displeasure, nor his fear. You panic brake, but it's too little too late ... the car's tyres cannot cope. The car steps away from you and you scramble for control. You jerk the wheel this way and the other, trying desperately to avoid oversteering in your bid to keep the car on course. Either by virtue of your skills or via the aid of sheer dumb luck, you make it through. Your car continues to careen down the track, right on the edge of control. There it is again ... that feeling ... euphoria!

If that's what it means to be a "racing sim", well ... I'm all here for it.

Dirt Rally 2.0, gameplay wise, is a good successor to Dirt Rally 1. Almost everything has been touched on; most seeing an improvement because of it.

However... Racenet, the fact that your career progress is perma-linked to Racenet and the fact that Racenet is integral to the always-online DRM is completely unacceptable - especially when you consider that DR1 didn't have it and that this costs quite a bit more than DR1.

What are you trying to stop? Piracy? Ha! Pirates cracked the game in less than 72 hours and now you're just punishing the paying customers. It's seriously anti-consumer when the consumer is being limited and punished for the crimes of a very small minority.

And then there's the predatory monetization, with much of the previous games' content being re-packaged as fairly-expensive DLC. If I wanted the old content; I'd play the old game. Where's the new stuff?

Ugh. If they at least fix this BS with Racenet, and I'll change my review and re-buy the game, but otherwise; I cannot recommend this game to anyone.

I cannot speak to playing on a controller as I haven't tried it, but with a wheel in VR it doesn't get much better. I played a lot of DR1 with the OG Vive/Revive and it was amazing for its time. Not going to go into all the details of pros/cons of the 2 games as others have done it better already. After i got this though I have uninstalled the first one and will not be going back. I am on a 2080 Ti and this game runs super smooth in VR on near max settings on everything. I run this game with no HUD in VR and the immersion is so good. Just going to say that if you have a newer gen VR headset and a nice wheel setup you will enjoy this game. Highly recommend.

A fantastic blend between simulation and arcade. Driving feels amazing, even on the Xbox One controller--especially on the gravel stages. As others have said, tarmac is not perfect; the rough surfaces are where Dirt Rally 2.0 shines. The career mode is engaging and just challenging enough, whilst the free time trials and custom competitions are always there in case you want freedom to choose exactly where and what you drive.

Like:
- Car feels very realistic on rough surfaces, even on a controller
- Graphics are great and locations look stunning. Sometimes I want to pull over to appreciate the view
- Sound is awesome: sharp and realistic, from the cars to the pacenotes
- Slick menus make the whole experience fluid and streamlined

What's missing:
- Dynamic weather / time would add more variety (only fixed presets are available)
- DLC is reasonably-priced and high-quality, but not having purchased a certain car or stage can prevent you from accessing daily/weekly challenges which is a shame. Would be great if there were more "stock" options in the community challenges
- Save replay would be great, avoiding having to screen capture to save a great run

tldr.text: Very Positive (89%): players praise the graphics and art.
The most common complaints are bugs and crashes, and the price.

details.text: Players who have logged few hours are far less positive than veterans, at 56% positive versus 94%.
For buyers now, server outages are a real risk: 6% of reviews complain about servers and matchmaking, and one says "you can't play half the game if the servers are down".
